newsitem.title: USA: ADM shares drop on probe concern - analysts.
newsitem.headline: ADM shares drop on probe concern - analysts.

text.p: Shares of Archer Daniels Midland Co traded lower Wednesday on concern that it will face charges after three other firms signed plea agreements in the U.S. goverment's probe of alleged fixing of lysine prices.
ADM was off 3/8 at 17-3/4 with 523,000 shares traded.
"The market is definitely (saying), 'This can't be good news for ADM'," Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said.

Ajinomoto Co Inc, Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd and the U.S. unit of Sewon Co Ltd of South Korea have signed plea agreements to charges in the probe of lysine, a feed additive. The probe also includes ADM.
The three companies also agreed to cooperate fully with the investigation by providing witnesses and documents.
"The fact that the foreign companies have agreed to cooperate in the government case (makes the market) nervous what that might mean to ADM," Wittenburg added.

Natwest Securities analyst David Nelson said in a report that pleas and cooperation from the alleged co-conspirators is "clearly a negative blow for the company's (ADM's) prospects in these legal proceedings."
But he added that the key investment issue for ADM remains negative fundamentals for the grain and oilseed processing giant.
"Excess industry capacity and constrained corn and soybean supplies suggest continued challenges to near-term earnings growth," Nelson said.
